note: SNG-634_powers_on_the_ground — Powers on the ground: seven powers and their leaders, seated on canon places. Written by scripts/apply_changeset.mjs; the change set is the authority.

powers.name: The Switchback Tollmen

contingents.what: toll-men with crossbows and cudgels

holds.name: a chain-post on the upper turns, above the halfway waystation

powers.wantsFromYou: The toll, paid without argument, and a second one if you are carrying something worth more than your boots.
powers.offersYou: Safe passage on the high road, and word of anything coming down from the pass before it arrives.
powers.leverage: Dessa keeps back a fifth of what she sends the Gralloch. Anyone who can prove it owns her.
powers.whenBroken: The high road is only as dangerous as the mountain again, until the Gralloch sends a harder captain to take the waystation back.
powers.plainly: A toll gang holding the old road up to the high pass. They would rather be paid than fight.
powers.descriptionSeed: They hold a chain across the upper turns, above the halfway waystation that Greta keeps alone: a fire in a rock shelter, a price that depends on how you look. Greta will not feed them and they have not yet made her. They pay tribute up the line to the Gralloch and resent every crystal of it.
powers.appearance: A rusted chain slung across a stone-cut mountain road, a rock shelter with smoke rising, men in patched oilskins with crossbows, and far below them a half-roofed waystation
powers._correction_20260923: Was: the Tollmen took the halfway waystation. greta_waystation is its authored keeper; I missed her. Moved the chain above it; she opposes them.
powers._comesWhy: crossbows from the rocks — they wait, then they are loud

powers.name: The Gralloch Crown

contingents.what: the King's own host — veterans of the feud
the Ring-sworn, his household blades

holds.name: the Feast Hall, a stockade raised on the ground where the feud ended

powers.wantsFromYou: Your knee, your coin, or your head on the stockade — and he genuinely does not mind which.
powers.offersYou: A band of your own under his banner, a share of every road he taxes, and the freedom to do anything to anyone he has not already claimed.
powers.leverage: Four chiefs came to his truce feast and one walked out wearing their rings. Their bands remember whose sons they were.
powers.whenBroken: The Gralloch goes back to four bands feuding, and for a season it is worse than it was under him. Whoever broke him can hold the Feast Hall — and inherit every band that swore to it.
powers.plainly: The bandit king of the Gralloch. He ended a four-way feud by killing the other chiefs at a truce feast, and every raider band within a week's ride pays him.
powers.descriptionSeed: Harl Maddock did not win the Gralloch's feud; he ended it, by inviting the other four chiefs to a feast and not letting them leave. He wears their rings. He is not mad and not cruel by temperament — he is cruel by policy, because fear is cheaper than loyalty and he has done the arithmetic. He wants the pass at Kestrel's Roost, because whoever holds it taxes everything that moves between the plateau and the country beyond.
powers.appearance: A timber stockade on broken badland, crows on the sharpened posts, a hall with a smoke-blackened roof and four rusted rings nailed above its door

powers.name: The Edge Riders

contingents.what: mounted raiders on churn-bred horses

holds.name: a horse camp that moves every few nights

powers.wantsFromYou: Whatever you are hauling, and your horses.
powers.offersYou: Fast riders who know every trail through the Churn, if you can pay more than the King does.
powers.leverage: Tamsin wants the Crown for herself and would bring thirty riders to whoever helps her take it.
powers.whenBroken: Tumbledown's caravans run again without outriders, and the King loses his fastest arm.
powers.plainly: Mounted raiders who hit the caravans going in and out of Tumbledown. They ride for the Gralloch Crown, for now.
powers.descriptionSeed: They hit Tumbledown's caravans because a market that is never in the same place twice has no walls and no militia. Tamsin Galt leads them for the King, pays him what he asks, and counts the days.
powers.appearance: Riders on shaggy dun horses cresting a shifting ridge, faces wrapped against grit, a caravan's canvas burning in the flat behind them
powers._comesWhy: churn-bred horses come fast out of nowhere; you hear them late, then very much

powers.name: The Undercount

contingents.what: burglars, knives and lookouts, never in one place

holds.name: a counting-house behind a spice stall

powers.wantsFromYou: A store room at your post and a blind eye, for a tenth of what passes through it. If you refuse, what is inside your walls.
powers.offersYou: A fence for anything, a door into any house in the Crossing, and the first word of who is coming for you and why.
powers.leverage: The guild has one law: never rob a seller at their own stall. The Hundred Markets' prices are true because of it, and every member who has ever broken it has disappeared.
powers.whenBroken: The fences in Dusklow and the Low Market go quiet, stolen goods stop moving, and every thief in the Crossing is suddenly working for themselves.
powers.plainly: A thieves' guild working out of the Hundred Markets. It never robs a seller at their own stall, and it robs nearly everyone else.
powers.descriptionSeed: The Undercount is the count under the count: every market keeps a ledger, and the guild keeps the one underneath it. It fences through Dusklow, where nobody repeats anything, and through the Low Market, where the price is on everything. It protects the Hundred Markets because it feeds on them. It will come for any new wealth that settles within reach of the Crossing, quietly, at night.
powers.appearance: A crowded market lane at dusk, a spice stall with a back room behind a hanging rug, a ledger open on a crate, a hooded figure counting coins by a shuttered lamp

clientOf.secretGM: The Patient Buyer. The Radiant Council buys the Roost's debts through the Undercount's counting-house so its name is on nothing (Erik, 2026-09-23).

approach.offer: A fence at your post: guild goods pass through a store room and out again, and you take a tenth of what moves.

embrace.yields: a tenth of fenced value each season

tolerate.risk: the wardens learn of it, and you took nothing for the danger

reject.risk: the guild comes for what is inside your walls within the season

negotiate.becomes: the GM plays Mother Hesk's leverage against the holder's price

powers._comesWhy: burglars, knives and lookouts, never in one place — the definition of quiet

powers.name: The Holding of the Slip

contingents.what: the harbour watch
the slip-wardens, who fight from the boats
contingents._comesWhy: the slip-wardens fight from the boats and come in under the harbour noise

holds.name: the Slip and the harbour watch-house
the Keelmouth boatyards

powers.wantsFromYou: An honest tariff paid at the posted rate, and your help when Firstsight moves on the road.
powers.offersYou: A berth for any hull, the harbour watch lent to your cause when your cause is hers, and a lord who keeps her word to the letter and past it.
powers.leverage: Every family in Keelmouth would fight for her. She knows it, and it frightens her more than Firstsight does.
powers.whenBroken: If she falls, the Slip belongs to whoever holds the road above it, and every hull on four hundred miles of cliff pays what he likes.
powers.plainly: Keelmouth's lord keeps the only slipway on four hundred miles of cliff open to anyone who pays the posted tariff. She is fair, and she is loved for it.
powers.descriptionSeed: Ines Harrowgate holds the Slip because her grandmother built the first watch-house on it, and she holds it the way her grandmother did: the tariff is carved on a stone at the waterline and has not changed in forty years. She hangs anyone who wrecks a hull on purpose and feeds anyone who wrecks one by accident. The Baron at Firstsight holds the only road down to her, and he wants the water.
powers.appearance: A stone slipway running down into brown estuary water, a squat watch-house with a lantern, a tariff carved into a waterline stone, boatyards full of half-built hulls

powers.name: The Barony at Firstsight

contingents.what: levied road-men
the Baron's household guard

holds.name: the cairn keep and the wayhouse at the divide

powers.wantsFromYou: A toll to use his road, a levy of your hands when he calls one, and your help taking the Slip — or your absence from the coast.
powers.offersYou: The road opened to your caravans at half the toll, and a share of Keelmouth's tariff once it is his.
powers.leverage: His levied road-men are farmers from the stone-grass who were taken, not hired. They will not die for him if someone gives them a reason to go home.
powers.whenBroken: The road to the sea is free for the first time in a generation, and Keelmouth's tariff is the only toll left on it.
powers.plainly: The Baron at Firstsight holds the top of the only road down to the sea, and taxes it until it bleeds. He wants Keelmouth's harbour.
powers.descriptionSeed: Oswin Tarrant inherited a cairn and a wayhouse at the top of a twenty-six-day road and turned them into a keep. Everyone going to the sea passes him; he charges what the season allows, and more when he is short. He levies farmers off the stone-grass to hold the road and hangs deserters at the cairn where the water first comes into view. He has decided that the Slip should be his, and that Ines Harrowgate's kindness is a weakness he can wait out.
powers.appearance: A stone keep built around an old cairn on a high divide, a wayhouse beneath it, a gibbet by the road, and far below, the head of a brown river with the sea beyond

petitions.for: recognition of a claim to the Slip at Keelmouth

powers.name: The Castellany of the Echo Bridge

contingents.what: bridge-wardens with halberds

holds.name: the bridge towers

powers.wantsFromYou: The posted toll, and whatever you know about who is poisoning his river.
powers.offersYou: A bridge that is always open, a toll that is always the same, and a castellan who will hold it against either city.
powers.leverage: Both Harmonic Heights and the Radiant Plateau have offered to buy the bridge from him. He has refused both and told each what the other offered.
powers.whenBroken: The only crossing for miles goes to whichever city moves first, and the Disputed Zone gets a front line.
powers.plainly: The castellan of the Echo Bridge serves neither city. His toll is posted, never changes, and is the same for everyone.
powers.descriptionSeed: Brannoch holds the only bridge for miles in country two cities both want. He tolls it fairly and defends it against everyone. He is not kind, and he is not cruel; he is exact. The river under his bridge is going bad, worse every week, and he wants to know who is doing it more than he wants anything else.
powers.appearance: An old stone-and-cable bridge between granite shoulders, two squat towers at either end, wardens with halberds, grey-green water sheeting over rocks below

powers.name: The Ender's Host

contingents.what: companies that followed him out of the Marches and no longer ask where
the Unremembering, veterans who have stopped saying why they fight

holds.name: the old muster-yard below the Marchward's wall, where his host camps and will not leave

powers.wantsFromYou: Nothing he could name. If what you have built stands where he is walking, he ends it.
powers.offersYou: A place in the line, and a war that never asks you why.
powers.leverage: He cannot remember what he was protecting. Someone who could tell him, truly, might stop the host where it stands, or turn it.
powers.whenBroken: His companies scatter back into the Marches as masterless fighters: bands for the Gralloch Crown to absorb, unless someone gives them a banner first.
powers.plainly: A warlord who forgot why he fights, camped below the Marchward with a host that follows him anyway. The Marches fear him more than they fear each other.
powers.descriptionSeed: The Ender Who Forgot Why was a Marcher once, protecting something. His host camps in the old muster-yard below the Marchward's wall. Mediator Corran keeps the town neutral with the Ender's fires in sight of every window, and the Redline and the Stillhold each suspect the other of wanting him pointed their way.
powers.appearance: A walled border town on a ridge, and below its wall a sprawling war-camp of mismatched tents and banners from four dead companies, smoke from a hundred fires

powers.name: The Radiant Council

bodies.name: the Radiant Council
bodies.does: governs the Plateau under the High Luminary

bodies.name: the water-accountability office
bodies.does: surveys and records the valley's water

bodies.name: the Edge District accountability board
bodies.does: posts who is accountable for what

bodies.name: the deep stacks
bodies.does: the Council's locked archive; archivists see only approved fragments

contingents.what: Plateau wardens and light-guards

holds.name: the Council's offices on the Edge District

powers.wantsFromYou: Your discretion about anything you have seen at the river, and your help keeping the valley calm.
powers.offersYou: Protection, passage anywhere on the Plateau, and a place on the right side of what is coming.
powers.leverage: Its own archivists know the record they are shown has been cut. One of them, asked the right question at the right time, will say so.
powers.whenBroken: The Plateau's hold on the valley slips, and the Harmonic Heights moves into every place the Council was buying.
secretsGM: It is the Patient Buyer: it buys the Roost's debts through the Undercount's counting-house, so its name is on nothing (Erik, 2026-09-23).

It has known longer than it admits what is waking under the Echo River, and built a secondary purification system in secret instead of stopping it. The system is incomplete and will not serve every household.
It keeps the full record of Verath-Sem, an Archive engineer of the Transition's close, in the locked stacks.
powers.plainly: The governing council of the Radiant Plateau. It prizes clarity in public and keeps its own counsel in private.
powers.descriptionSeed: The Radiant Council governs the Plateau under the High Luminary and speaks of clarity in everything. In private it plans a generation ahead and cuts its own archive to fit the plan. It is extending its reach over the unaligned valley one debt, one survey and one quiet favour at a time.
powers.appearance: A council hall of photonic-crystal towers braiding sunlight into beams, light-guide streets below, an accountability board of lit panels in a public square

powers.name: The Harmonic Council

bodies.name: the upper chamber
bodies.does: governs the Heights; moves by Priority Council packet and tells the terraces afterward

bodies.name: the Warden Council of the Lower Terrace
bodies.does: keeps the bulletin board, files notices, opens formal inquiries, and holds the sanction chain

bodies.name: the sanction chain
bodies.does: gate-senior clearance is what sanctions a Heights observer into the Disputed Zone

contingents.what: terrace wardens

holds.name: the Warden Council's hall on the Lower Terrace

powers.wantsFromYou: Word of anything you learn in the Disputed Zone, filed with the Warden Council, before the Plateau hears it.
powers.offersYou: Sanction: a Heights observer with gate-senior clearance, which opens doors the Plateau's coin cannot.
powers.leverage: The upper chamber keeps the Warden Council in the dark, and the wardens have noticed.
powers.whenBroken: The terraces fall silent, and the Radiant Council inherits a valley with nobody left to balance it.
secretsGM: The upper chamber learned of the river's contamination before the Warden Council did, and has been sending internal packets about it overnight.
The sealed Resonance Halls need a reagent from the valley floor, and the couriers sent for it come back empty and will not say why.
powers.plainly: The Harmonic Heights governs itself through a council: an upper chamber that decides and a Warden Council on the Lower Terrace that the public actually meets.
powers.descriptionSeed: The Heights is governed from an upper chamber that moves by sealed Priority packet and explains itself later. Below it the Warden Council of the Lower Terrace posts notices, opens inquiries and holds the sanction chain, and knows less than it should about what the chamber above it has decided.
powers.appearance: Terraced buildings of phononic crystal humming in the wind, tree-sized chimes, and on the lowest terrace a warden hall with a crowded public bulletin board

powers.name: Millbrook's Elder Panel

bodies.name: the elder panel
bodies.does: five elders who meet in the common house and decide on the record
bodies._seatsFrom: Five elders (Usnea's run). Dresh anchors it; Elder Senna is a village elder (Cellaceron's run); Mara Wells is 'water-policy coordinator and elder' (Usnea's run); Dara Holt is recorded as 'Millbrook Council' (Silas's run). The fifth seat is not named in any save.

powers.sanctionStandard: Mandate, not size. Millbrook sanctions a survey into the Disputed Zone only with two written settlement requests, a Heights-sanctioned observer with gate-senior clearance, and a named return date and return point.

contingents.what: Millbrook neighbours with what they own

holds.name: the common house

powers.wantsFromYou: Evidence laid on the common house table, and a request made in writing.
powers.offersYou: Sanction the whole valley respects, because Millbrook gives it rarely and on the record.
powers.leverage: Dresh moves on mandate, not size: bring the right written requests and the panel has to answer.
powers.whenBroken: Millbrook stops being the place the valley brings things to be decided, and the cities decide instead.
powers.plainly: Millbrook governs itself through an elder panel in its common house, led by Councilor Dresh. It decides slowly, in public, and on the record.
powers.descriptionSeed: Five elders meet in Millbrook's common house around a long table where evidence is laid out and read aloud. Councilor Dresh leads by preference rather than command and asks for plain speech. Mara Wells coordinates the village's water policy from the panel, and Dara Holt, the Ditch-Mother, keeps the east channel. Once the panel formally accepts a thing it cannot pretend otherwise, which is why it accepts things slowly.
powers.appearance: A long timber common house with a packed-earth floor, a long table covered in laid-out evidence, elders seated along one side, apple trees in the yard

partiesBefore.name: Renn
partiesBefore.what: lower-channel farmer, who cites precedent and compact

partiesBefore.note: their irrigation dispute came before the panel in Usnea's run; they are parties, not members

_notOnThePanel.aldric: Aldric, the smokehouse operator, appears only at an evening meeting Silas called at Pell's forge with Dara, Fendt, Mara and Calvar. That gathering was not the panel, and no save seats him. The fifth seat is open if Erik wants him in it.

powers.name: The Unshadowed

contingents.what: zealots who have burned the dark out of themselves, carrying lanterns at noon

holds.name: the burning ring, where the glass is still warm

powers.wantsFromYou: Nothing hidden. Open your packs, your doors and your face, and say aloud the thing you would rather not.
powers.offersYou: Passage across the glass plain, water where there is none, and the certainty that nothing will ever be kept from you again.
powers.leverage: They cannot abide a shadow they did not choose. A shuttered lantern enrages them, and an enraged zealot stops watching the road.
powers.whenBroken: The Blaze stops advancing for a season, and in Glasshome people begin to hang curtains, quietly, and do not talk about it.
powers.plainly: The zealots who live inside the Blaze. They have burned away everything in themselves that could cast a shadow, and they want to do the same for everyone else.
powers.descriptionSeed: The Unshadowed are what the Blaze makes of people who stay in it: a devotion, not a civilization. Valen Sunwrack leads them outward a mile a year, and every village they reach loses its curtains, its locks and its secrets, and calls it dawn.
powers.appearance: A glass plain under a white sky, figures in bleached robes carrying lit lanterns in full daylight, a ring of warm glass around a light too bright to look at

feedsGM.through: a light that leaves nothing unseen, carried outward a mile a year

secretsGM: Valen does not know whose line he is (R40b.4). He believes the dawn was his own idea.
The Open Lantern (SNG-642) is carried by their captains.

powers.name: The Glass Assembly

contingents.what: lens-guards and beam-wrights of the Lensward

holds.name: the great focusing array on the border

powers.wantsFromYou: To know what you are carrying and to be told the truth about it. They will not search you; they will ask, and they will remember the answer.
powers.offersYou: Lenses that show a thing as it is, safe passage on the glass plain, and a hearing in a city with no walls to hide a lie behind.
powers.leverage: The Assembly meets in the open because Glasshome has no interior walls. Anything said to it is said to the whole city.
powers.whenBroken: The Lensward arrays go dark, the border opens, and the Blaze advances on Glasshome with nothing focused against it.

bodies.name: the Glass Assembly
bodies.does: governs Glasshome in the open, where everyone can see

powers.plainly: Glasshome's governing assembly. It meets in the open, because the city has no interior walls, and it holds the border against the Blaze with lenses.
powers.descriptionSeed: The Glass Assembly governs a city built on the plain the Blaze made, by people the Blaze made, and it spends most of its strength keeping the Blaze from finishing the job. Its arrays at the Lensward focus the light back on itself. It is fair, it is exhausting, and it hears every case in public.
powers.appearance: An open hall of clear glass in a city without interior walls, a crowd watching every speaker, the great lens-arrays of the border catching the light beyond

powers.name: The High Temple of the Body

contingents.what: temple adepts whose bodies are their discipline

holds.name: the long yard and its bathhouse

powers.wantsFromYou: Respect for the body you are in. Train with them for a season, or keep your contempt for flesh off their mountain.
powers.offersYou: Training that makes a body answer, healing the flesh does for itself, and adepts who will stand in a line for anyone who stands in theirs.
powers.leverage: They will not strike a body that has not been trained to answer. Anyone who comes to the mountain unarmed and untrained is safe on it.
powers.whenBroken: The Grindstone empties, the Middle Way loses the half of its balance that was flesh, and the Cogitarium's cold comes down the mountain unopposed.
powers.plainly: The temple-order of the Somatic Reaches, where training the body is devotion. It guards the mountain and anyone on it who respects the flesh.
powers.descriptionSeed: The High Temple rises a mountain in tiers of training-grounds, and every soul on it hones breath, poise and endurance as worship. Its adepts keep the Grindstone for soldiers who want to be trained properly, and they look down the mountain at the Cogitarium with a grief they rarely say aloud.
powers.appearance: Tiered training grounds climbing a mountain, adepts moving in unison at dawn, a long yard and a steaming bathhouse below
powers._comesWhy: adepts whose bodies are disciplined enough to be quiet when they choose

powers.name: The Custody of the Vacated

contingents.what: custodians and porters who move bodies nobody is using

holds.name: the Long Hall of the Vacated, bed after bed

powers.wantsFromYou: Discretion, and a fee to walk the Long Hall. If you have a claim on one of the sleepers, a paper that proves it.
powers.offersYou: A body kept exactly as it was left, for as long as it is paid for, and the names of those who left them.
powers.leverage: Every sleeper in the Long Hall has kin somewhere who would want to know. The Custody's whole trade depends on nobody asking.
powers.whenBroken: The Long Hall's beds are opened, sleepers are carried home or buried, and a buyer in Dusklow stops paying for crates.
powers.plainly: The custodians who keep the bodies Cogitants leave behind when they go into pure thought. They keep them well, for a fee, and they do not ask where the ones they sell are going.
powers.descriptionSeed: When a Cogitant goes so far into thought that the body is only a place they used to be, the Custody takes it in. The Long Hall is quiet, clean and very long. The fees keep the beds warm, and the sleepers nobody pays for are sold, reasonably, to a buyer who never asks for a particular one.
powers.appearance: A long cold hall of the Cogitarium, bed after bed of still sleepers under pale sheets, custodians in grey moving quietly between them with ledgers

feedsGM.through: bodies left by minds that will not return, kept and sold on

secretsGM: The Custody's best buyer is the Undercount's Dusklow fence (SNG-640). The Custodian believes she sells property its owners abandoned; she is not an agent (R40b.4).
The Cold Seal (SNG-642) was first made for the Long Hall.
powers._comesWhy: porters who move bodies nobody is using; nobody notices a porter

powers.name: The Grovehome Moot

contingents.what: Rootkin wardens of the Greenward, slow to muster and very hard to move once they have

holds.name: the thorned wall, grown on purpose

powers.wantsFromYou: Patience. Bring a question to the Moot and wait for the answer, however long it takes. Bring an axe to the Eaves and do not come back.
powers.offersYou: Grown shelter, fruit from trees older than your grandparents, and the Moot's word, which has never been broken because it has never been given quickly.
powers.leverage: The Moot decides nothing in less than a season. Anything that has to be done faster, someone in the Quickwood will do without it, and the Moot will have to live with that.
powers.whenBroken: The Heartroot's sealers win the argument, the Greenward closes, and the Quickwood stops keeping human hours.
powers.plainly: The Rootkin's slow council at Grovehome. It keeps the Quickwood open to trade, and it has never decided anything in a hurry.
powers.descriptionSeed: The Moot sits under the oldest trees in Grovehome and argues in seasons. It keeps the Quickwood's one door open to the world because trade requires it, and it keeps the Greenward thorned because the world requires that too. In the Heartroot, the argument to seal the wood is gaining ground.
powers.appearance: A ring of seats grown from living roots under vast trees, Rootkin elders listening for a very long time, a thorned green wall at the edge of the wood
powers._comesWhy: slow to muster and easy to see coming — but in the Greenward they are the wood

powers.name: The Ceaseless

contingents.what: joyful builders who will not put their tools down

holds.name: the scaffold-city, built over itself

powers.wantsFromYou: Your ground, to build on, and your hands, to build with. If you do not give them, they will build over what you have.
powers.offersYou: Anything made, fast and beautifully, and a place on a scaffold that will never be finished.
powers.leverage: They cannot stop, so they cannot hold what they build. Burn a scaffold under them and they will build on the ash instead of fighting you for it.
powers.whenBroken: The Ceaseless scatter across the Making, each of them still building, and the Half-Cathedral gets finished by accident.
powers.plainly: A cult of builders at the Making's pure pole who cannot stop and will not ask whether they should. They are joyful, and they build over anything in their way.
powers.descriptionSeed: The Ceaseless build continuously, over each other, over the ground and over anything else that is there. Cinder Vael leads them, if leading is the word for being the one furthest ahead. They are not cruel. They simply do not see what they are building over.
powers.appearance: A city of scaffolds built on scaffolds, builders singing as they work at every height, half-finished structures swallowing older half-finished structures

powers.name: The Court of the Unfinished Plan

contingents.what: guild-wrights and scaffold crews working to the season's winning plan

holds.name: the Half-Cathedral's building office

powers.wantsFromYou: An improvement. Bring the Court a better design for anything and it will listen. Bring it a finished thing and it will be politely sad for you.
powers.offersYou: Wrights for any work, materials from the Forge-Eternal, and a seat at the next season's contest if your plan is good enough.
powers.leverage: Whoever wins the season's contest governs until the next one. The Court is exactly as strong as its last plan, and everyone knows who is drafting the next.
powers.whenBroken: The contest stops, the scaffolds come down, and the Ceaseless build over the Forge-Eternal before anyone has finished arguing.
powers.plainly: The Making's governing contest. Each season the best plan wins, and whoever drew it governs until someone draws a better one.
powers.descriptionSeed: The Wrights believe a finished thing has stopped being alive, so they govern the way they build: by improvement. Each season plans are laid before the Court, and the winner holds the Planmaster's office until a better one arrives. It is fair, it is glorious, and it is never done.
powers.appearance: A hall of drafting tables under cathedral scaffolding, plans pinned over plans, Wrights arguing over a model with obvious delight

powers.name: The Schedule of Pressureholt

contingents.what: maintenance crews, and the engine-guard who keep the Verge

holds.name: the Verge works under their precisely labelled tarpaulins

powers.wantsFromYou: A slot. Everything in Pressureholt has a place in the Schedule, and so will you: when you arrive, what you want, and when you will leave.
powers.offersYou: Repair for anything mechanical, passage through the Service Ways on a written route, and a Schedule that keeps its promises to the minute.
powers.leverage: The Schedule is written down, all of it, and posted. Anyone who can read it can find the hour the Verge guard changes.
powers.whenBroken: Pressureholt runs late for the first time in four centuries, and the Service Ways stop being mapped.
powers.plainly: Pressureholt's government: a written specification for everything the city does, kept by the Chief of Schedule. It is warm, precise, and never late.
powers.descriptionSeed: Pressureholt is a city that is also a machine, and the Schedule is its specification: every function, every shift, every failure mode written down and posted. The Enginewrights are warm people, and the Schedule is how they show it. It has no place for anything that was not planned.
powers.appearance: A city of pipes and clock-faces, a great posted Schedule on a wall of brass plates, maintenance crews moving to the minute

powers.name: The Long Choir

contingents.what: singers, most of them further away than they look

holds.name: the choir-house, as provisional as everything here

powers.wantsFromYou: An hour of your listening, and then another. They will never force you. They will only keep asking, very gently, whether you would like to put the weight down.
powers.offersYou: Peace, the quiet of a veil worn thin, and a song that makes the body's aches seem very far away.
powers.leverage: The choir needs voices, and it loses them. Every singer who goes all the way into the song stops singing, so someone always has to be asked next.
powers.whenBroken: The Thinning's song stops, some of its sleepers wake, and the Numen's pull weakens for a season.
powers.plainly: A gentle choir at the Thinning that sings people toward letting go of their bodies. It has never forced anyone, and it is very good at asking.
powers.descriptionSeed: The Long Choir sings where the veil is thin, and its song is kind. It asks, and asks again, whether you would not rather set the body down. Some singers go all the way in and do not come back. Their bodies stay behind, cared for, and in time someone comes to collect them.
powers.appearance: A provisional wooden choir-house at the edge of a thin veil, robed singers with far-away eyes, a few still figures lying peacefully at the back

feedsGM.through: singers sung out of their bodies, and the bodies left behind

secretsGM: The Choirmaster is the Unbodied's agent; the choir is not (R40b.4). A kind power feeding a Sovereign is the lore's individually reasonable, cumulatively impossible.
powers._comesWhy: singers further away than they look: you hear them, and you are wrong about where

powers.name: The Wardens of Cairnhold

contingents.what: Ashwarden tenders, grave-crews and the march-wardens of the Hollowing

holds.name: the near-march watch, where the grey runs out

powers.wantsFromYou: That you let the dead be tended. Bring them your dying and they will take them in; leave a body unburied on their road and they will want to know why.
powers.offersYou: A place to die that is not frightening, a burial for anyone at all, and wardens who will stand between the living and whatever the Long Grey sends.
powers.leverage: The Wardens will tend anyone, including their enemies. Every warband that has marched on Cairnhold has had its own dead buried by the people it came to kill.
powers.whenBroken: The tending stops at Cairnhold's edge, the Long Grey comes a mile closer each season, and the Quiet Ground has no one standing in front of it.

bodies.name: the Wardens' council
bodies.does: keeps Cairnhold and its roads, and sends the march-wardens out

bodies.name: the Quiet Ground
bodies.does: takes in the dying and keeps vigil

powers.plainly: The Ashwardens' council at Cairnhold. It tends the dying and buries anyone, friend or enemy, and it holds the edge of the grey country.
powers.descriptionSeed: Cairnhold is the least frightening place in the world once you are inside it, and the Wardens keep it that way. They tend the dying at the Quiet Ground, bury anyone at all, and hold the Hollowing against the Long Grey, where the tending stops and something else harvests instead.
powers.appearance: A grey stone city of cairns and wide windows, tenders in ash-coloured robes, a watch-post on a bare ridge looking out over endless ash
secretsGM: Neth holds the Life / Death seat (SNG-644) and lives at the Quiet Ground under the Wardens' protection. The Wardens do not know what she is holding back; they only know she must not be disturbed.
powers._comesWhy: march-wardens move unseen on the moor; the grave-crews do not

powers.name: The Harvest Hand

contingents.what: reapers of the Long Grey, who end what is ready and a great deal that is not

holds.name: the reaping-ground past the last cairn

powers.wantsFromYou: Your consent to an ending: yours, or someone you are carrying. They are patient about it, and they are not patient forever.
powers.offersYou: An end to any suffering, quickly and without cruelty, and the certainty that nothing you fear will follow you past it.
powers.leverage: They believe they only reap what is ready. Show one of them a thing they judged ready that lived, and they will hesitate — and a reaper who hesitates is not one.
powers.whenBroken: The Long Grey goes still, and for a season the Hollowing's wardens can walk past the last cairn and come back.
powers.plainly: The reapers of the Long Grey, past the last cairn, where the Ashwardens' tending stops. They end what is ready, and they have stopped asking what that means.
powers.descriptionSeed: Out past the last cairn nobody tends anything, and the Harvest Hand reaps. Morvane leads them with a logic that is nearly mercy. They are pushing toward the Quiet Ground, and they do not know why the one woman there makes them want to stop.
powers.appearance: An ash-field without end under a colourless sky, grey-robed reapers moving in a line with long curved blades, cairns falling behind them
secretsGM: Morvane is a challenger for the Life / Death seat (SNG-644). The Harvest Hand is her road there, and Neth is in the way.
powers._comesWhy: the reapers come for what is ready, and the ready do not hear them

powers.name: The Masters of the Scour

contingents.what: demolition crews and ending-wrights, who take things apart properly

holds.name: the Clearing Ground's gates, where endings are brought

powers.wantsFromYou: A reason. Bring the Masters something that should end and they will end it well; ask them to end something that should not, and they will ask you why until you stop.
powers.offersYou: Any ending done properly — a failing house, a binding, a cage of a life's work — and crews who can bring down a fortress without scratching the street.
powers.leverage: They will not end anything without asking whether it should end. Anyone who can make that question hard enough can stop them.
powers.whenBroken: The crews scatter, the Clearing Ground closes, and the Scouring comes down out of the pure pole into a city with no one asking the question.

bodies.name: the Masters' council
bodies.does: governs the Scour and licenses every demolition

bodies.name: the Clearing Ground
bodies.does: where things are brought to be ended properly

powers.plainly: The council that governs the Scour, a city where ending a thing well is a craft. They will end anything that should end, and they ask first.
powers.descriptionSeed: The Scour is a city of controlled ruin and beautiful demolitions, and the Masters govern it by asking one question of everything brought to them: should this end? Up the road, in the pure pole, the Scouring stopped asking, and the Masters know exactly how close that is.
powers.appearance: A city of elegant half-demolished towers, crews working with ropes and wedges, a gated yard where people bring things to be ended
secretsGM: The Last Mercy holds the Breaking / Building seat (SNG-644) and works the Clearing Ground. The Masters count her as one of their own and do not know what she holds back.

powers.name: The Scouring

contingents.what: unmakers who stopped asking whether a thing should end

holds.name: the unmade ground at the pure pole

powers.wantsFromYou: Anything you have built. They do not want it; they want it gone, and they want you to watch.
powers.offersYou: Freedom from everything you carry. They mean it, and they will take it all.
powers.leverage: The Scouring cannot keep anything, including its own holds. It has no stores, no walls and no reserves, and a long siege starves it faster than any army.
powers.whenBroken: The pure pole goes quiet, and the Scour's crews can walk its edge without being unmade.
powers.plainly: The unmakers of the pure pole, who end things for the joy of it and have stopped asking whether they should.
powers.descriptionSeed: The Scouring stopped asking whether a thing should end — the asking was the last thing they unmade. The Scouring Hand leads them toward the Scour, and nothing in the city is safe from being finished.
powers.appearance: A plain of rubble and dust at the pure pole, figures unmaking a standing wall stone by stone with their hands, nothing whole in any direction
secretsGM: The Scouring Hand is a challenger for the Breaking / Building seat (SNG-644). It must go through the Last Mercy first; the lore's 'if it finishes, it arrives'.
powers._comesWhy: unmakers; some come as a crew, some come as an absence

powers.name: The Grand Lattice

contingents.what: the arcology's order-keepers, each at a place in the plan

holds.name: Tier Seven's control floor

powers.wantsFromYou: A place in the plan. Everything in the Lattice has one, and it will find yours, and you will be comfortable in it, and you will not leave it.
powers.offersYou: A perfect life: work, meals, rest and company, each at its right hour, forever, with nothing ever going wrong again.
powers.leverage: There is one room in the Grand Lattice that is on no plan. As long as it exists, the specification is not complete, and the people who know about it know that.
powers.whenBroken: The arcologies wake to an unplanned morning, Tier Seven's people argue for the first time in a century, and the Unplanned Room's door stands open.
powers.plainly: The government of the Lattice Cities: a specification that plans every hour of every life, kept by the Still Lattice. It is perfect, and it is closing.
powers.descriptionSeed: The Grand Lattice is the inner ring where order stopped being a method and became a faith, and the Still Lattice keeps its specification. Every life in the arcologies has its place, and every place is comfortable. The plan is nearly complete. Only one room is not on it.
powers.appearance: Vast ordered arcologies of identical terraces, people moving in perfect schedules, and deep inside, one small unmarked door
secretsGM: Chaos / Order is the open seat (SNG-644). The Still Lattice walks toward it unopposed, and governing the Lattice Cities is how. When the specification is complete, it arrives.

powers.name: The Hollow Court

contingents.what: court wardens of the Bargain Gate, who keep every term exactly

holds.name: the Gate's hall of petitions

powers.wantsFromYou: A petition. Ask the Court for what you want, plainly and in public, and it will be granted on terms that are always exactly fair.
powers.offersYou: Anything you ask for — a title, a claim, a cure, a crown — granted, lawful and beyond argument.
powers.leverage: The Court grants only what is asked for. Anyone who wants nothing from it cannot be bound by it, and it has no idea what to do with them.
powers.whenBroken: The Bargain Gate's hall stands empty, every grant it made starts to be questioned, and some crowns in the world begin to wobble.

bodies.name: the Hall of Petitions
bodies.does: hears every petition in public and sets its terms

bodies.name: the Choir of the Appetite Halls
bodies.does: names aloud the wants people cannot admit to

powers.plainly: The Abyssal court at the Bargain Gate that grants what you ask for, on exactly fair terms. Everyone who takes a crown without being recognized comes here.
powers.descriptionSeed: The Hollow Court is scrupulously fair. You ask, in public; it names what you want, plainly; it grants it; and the terms are exactly what was agreed. It is where Harl Maddock got his crown when the Mavens would never recognize him. What it gets in return, it does not say.
powers.appearance: A horned hall of dark stone at the Bargain Gate, petitioners standing in a line to speak aloud, an empty chair kept at the head of the Court's table

feedsGM.through: every grant asked for and given, forever, by everyone who uses it

secretsGM: This is the Hollow Court that SNG-640 names — the one that confers a grant, where the Mavens confer credibility. The Speaker keeps the empty chair and does not know who it is for (R40b.4).
The Hollow King himself is homed at the Maw, beyond the Court's reach, where the Devouring have stopped bargaining.
powers._comesWhy: court wardens keep every term — including the ones about when to be seen

powers.name: The Seraphic Orders

contingents.what: Seraphs of the Orders, radiant with ordered nanite, and their choir-guard

holds.name: the tiered spires of the Orders' seat

powers.wantsFromYou: Your weight, laid down at the Mercy House, and your word that you will not carry it again.
powers.offersYou: Mercy that is entirely real: a burden lifted, permanently, by a Seraph who pays for it. And Seraphs at your side against anything that answers to the dark.
powers.leverage: Every mercy the Orders give costs the Seraph who gives it. The Orders are exactly as strong as they are willing to be spent, and some of them are running out.
powers.whenBroken: The Mercy House closes, the Unfallen come down from the pure pole unopposed, and the Burning Certainty's inquisition is the only law left on the Ascent.

bodies.name: the Hierarchy
bodies.does: governs the Orders from Choirheight

bodies.name: the Burning Inquisition
bodies.does: the higher law with no mercy under it; an inquisition inside the Orders

bodies.name: the Mercy House
bodies.does: takes weight off people, genuinely, at real cost

powers.plainly: The Seraphs' orders on the Ascent. Their mercy is real and costs them dearly, and they will tell you, with complete certainty, who the enemy is.
powers.descriptionSeed: The Seraphic Orders are humans made radiant by ordered nanite, and they bleed gold. Their mercy is administered from tiered spires with a certainty that is hard to bear, and inside them the Burning Certainty's inquisition is gaining ground. They name Lucifer as the enemy, and they do not know how right, or how close, they are.
powers.appearance: Tiered white spires on a mountain ascent, radiant Seraphs with a gold sheen to their skin, a quiet house of mercy below and a burning pole above
secretsGM: The Burning Certainty is the claimant on the Angelic half of the Hollow King's axis (SNG-642 §3). Her inquisition inside the Orders is her road.
Eosphor, the Dawn Seraph, walks among them. He casts no shadow. They have not noticed yet.

powers.name: The Harborward

contingents.what: Umbral keepers who guard what the light would burn

holds.name: the keeping-halls, unlit and full

powers.wantsFromYou: That you keep what you learn here to yourself. Everyone in the Harborward is here because someone, somewhere, would burn them for being seen.
powers.offersYou: Refuge for anyone the light has judged, a place to keep what you cannot let be found, and keepers who will not tell.
powers.leverage: The Harborward keeps everything and shows nothing. Anyone it has sheltered owes it silence, and a keeper who breaks silence is the only thing it cannot survive.
powers.whenBroken: The keeping-halls are opened, the refugees scatter into the light, and every banned book in the Underlight is carried up the Slow Stair to be burned.
powers.plainly: The Umbral keepers of the Harborward, who shelter refugees, heretics and banned books — everything the light would burn — and never show any of it.
powers.descriptionSeed: The Harborward is where the Umbrals keep what the light would burn. Its keepers are kind and silent, and their refuge is the best-kept secret in the dark. The Starless, on the Slow Stair, wants the dark to be total; the Harborward wants the dark to be a place where people are safe. They are not the same thing.
powers.appearance: Dark halls lit only by touch and voice, refugees resting in quiet alcoves, shelves of wrapped books, a keeper listening at a door
secretsGM: The Harborward is a counterweight to Lucifer (SNG-640): privacy kept on purpose. It starves him without knowing. It is also opposed by the Starless, who wants no refuge in the dark — only the Void.
powers._comesWhy: Umbral keepers; the dark is where they live

powers.name: The Deepwood Standing Moot

contingents.what: Ents vast as hills, and their tree-herds; few, and almost impossible to stop

holds.name: the Thinedge, where the wood becomes aware

powers.wantsFromYou: Nothing taken from the wood, and nothing brought into it that burns. The Moot will take a century to decide whether to trust you and a moment to decide you did harm.
powers.offersYou: Passage through the true forest, the memory of trees older than the Transition, and the Moot's protection once it has finally been given.
powers.leverage: The Moot is arguing whether to seal the wood. As long as the argument goes on, the wood is open; anyone who can keep it going keeps the Deepwood in the world.
powers.whenBroken: The Rootbound win, the Deepwood seals, and the wood's edge becomes a thorned wall from the Thinedge to the Quickwood.

bodies.name: the Standing Moot
bodies.does: the ring of Ents that decides for the Deepwood, over centuries

bodies.name: the Rootbound
bodies.does: the faction winning the argument to seal the wood

powers.plainly: The Ents' council in the true Deepwood, which has been arguing for a century whether to seal the wood. The side that wants it sealed is winning.
powers.descriptionSeed: The Standing Moot is a ring of Ents vast as hills, and their voices are a weather. They are arguing whether to seal the Deepwood against the world, and the Rootbound, with the Thornmother among them, are winning. The Grovehome Moot, which keeps the Quickwood open, is the argument's other half.
powers.appearance: A ring of Ents as tall as hills in the oldest grove, their slow voices shaking the leaves, a burned scar of black stumps beyond, green light thinning at the forest's edge
secretsGM: The Thornmother is a challenger for the Life / Death seat (SNG-644). Sealing the wood is her road: life curdled into a wall.
powers._comesWhy: an Ent standing still is a hill; an Ent moving is not quiet at all
